hook: Ammonia made during nitrate reduction reshapes the copper catalyst that makes it.
hook_turn: reshapes the copper catalyst that makes it.
summary: Atomic force microscopy run during the reaction shows copper surfaces change shape in step with whether nitrite or ammonia is the main product. At higher voltage, fast ammonia formation grows copper islands rich in step sites, which the authors explain by copper dissolving and redepositing. The link between surface change and selectivity is a correlation under lab conditions on flat copper.
title: Ammonia-Driven Nanoscale Surface Restructuring of Copper Catalysts during Nitrate Reduction Reaction
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
